# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-2 (Extended v45)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion and Bombarda's restaurant); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; Valjean enters courtroom; WITNESSES TESTIFY; Valjean rises and reveals himself; DEPARTS COURTROOM; ARRIVES AT INFIRMARY NEXT MORNING AT DAYBREAK)**; 1862 (narrative reflection); present day (spring to late August/early September, England); future wedding (following spring); 1795 (Valjean's theft and trial)
- Primary locations: M. sur M., Montfermeil, Arras (Hotel de la Poste, Court of Assizes in Prefecture, council-chamber, courtroom with corridors, steps, gratings, door); infirmary (laboratory, Fantine's chamber); England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby); Secondary locations as previously detailed.
- **Journey and courtroom entry (completed)**: Valjean hired Scaufflaire's tilbury; departed M. sur M. night of January 1823; arrived Arras nearly eight o'clock evening; left alone in council-chamber; fled corridor in terror; re-entered courtroom despite fear; concealed face behind cardboard boxes; gradually recovered composure sufficient to listen.
- **Council-chamber hallucination (completed)**: 1795 condemnation machinery reified in present with formidable reality; crucifix above President's head (absent at 1795 trial); recognized apparatus of judgment that condemns.
- **Trial proceedings and testimony (completed)**: Champmathieu (accused) made incoherent denials; district-attorney demanded witness recall; Javert's absence acknowledged (called to neighboring arrondissement); district-attorney recited Javert's deposition in full (recognized Valjean as "very vicious," suspected of Bishop's theft, nineteen years penal servitude, five-six escape attempts); Ex-convict Brevet testified (age sixty, business face, prison rascal, religious habits, recognized Valjean as galley companion entered 1796 left 1815, acknowledged age brutalized him); Prisoner-for-life Chenildieu (brought from Toulon galleys, red cassock, green cap, fifty years old, brisk wrinkled frail yellow brazen-faced feverish, nicknamed "Je-nie Dieu," strong glance); Prisoner-for-life Cochepaille (red cassock, peasant from Lourdes, mountain shepherd turned brigand, savage); Champmathieu's reactions: astounded face, muttered satisfaction at testimonies.
- **Valjean's courtroom revelation (completed)**: Man (Valjean) rose among privileged spectators, pushed through half-door, stood in middle of hall; President, district-attorney, M. Bamatabois, twenty persons recognized him and exclaimed in concert; Valjean very pale, trembled slightly, hat in hand, coat carefully buttoned; **his gray hair had turned entirely white during the hour he sat in courtroom**; clerk's lamp illumined countenance; audience experienced indescribable sensation, momentary hesitation (could not believe tranquil man uttered heart-rending cry); indecision lasted seconds only.
- **Valjean's address to court (completed)**: Before President and district-attorney could speak or ushers/gendarmes gesture, Valjean advanced towards witnesses Cochepaille, Brevet, Chenildieu; interrupted district-attorney with suavity and authority; addressed Chenildieu directly: "you who conferred on yourself the name of 'Jenie-Dieu,' your whole right shoulder bears a deep burn, because you one day laid your shoulder against the chafing-dish full of coals, in order to efface the three letters T. F. P., which are still visible, nevertheless; answer, is this true?" (Words literally written down immediately after trial by witness, ringing in ears of those who heard them nearly forty years ago.)
- **Courtroom transformation and Valjean's departure (completed)**: Chamber contained no longer judges, accusers, gendarmes; only staring eyes and sympathizing hearts; no one recalled part they might play; district-attorney forgot prosecuting purpose, President presiding purpose, counsel defending purpose; no question put, no authority intervened; all experienced sublime spectacle that captured souls, turned witnesses into spectators; all felt inwardly dazzled; Valjean directed steps towards door; not a voice raised, not an arm extended to hinder; all stood aside; divine something about him caused multitudes to stand aside and make way; traversed crowd slowly; never known who opened door; he found door open upon reaching it; turned round upon arriving (sentence incomplete in text).
- **Infirmary scene—next morning at daybreak (completed)**: Fantine passed sleepless, feverish night filled with happy visions; fell asleep at daybreak; Sister Simplice watching, went to prepare chinchona potion in laboratory; Valjean entered silently, appeared before sister; sister explained Fantine had been very ill previous day, better now thinking mayor gone to Montfermeil for child; sister perceived plainly from his air he had not come from there; sister suggested not informing Fantine of Madeleine's return until child arrived, to spare her disappointment and avoid enacted lie; Valjean made remarks about badly shutting door that might awaken sick woman; entered Fantine's chamber, approached bed, drew aside curtains; Fantine asleep, breathing with tragic sound peculiar to terminal maladies; countenance overspread with ineffable serenity, transfigured in sleep; pallor become whiteness, cheeks crimson, long golden lashes (only remaining beauty of youth and virginity) palpitated though closed; whole person trembling with indescribable unfolding of wings ready to bear her away; resembled something on point of soaring away rather than dying; Valjean remained motionless beside bed, gazing upon sick woman and crucifix as done two months before on first visit; same attitude—she sleeping, he praying; difference: **after two months, her hair gray, his hair white**.

## Main Characters and Relationships

**Jean Valjean / M. Madeleine—IDENTITY REVEALED, PAST CONFRONTED, NOW AT FANTINE'S BEDSIDE**
- Witnessed trial in council-chamber then courtroom; experienced hallucination of 1795 condemnation reified; hair turned white during hour of trial attendance; rose dramatically to reveal himself to entire court; addressed Chenildieu with specific knowledge of burn mark and T.F.P. letters (personal galley knowledge); departed courtroom with divine something causing crowd to part; appeared next morning at infirmary at daybreak; gazes upon Fantine; his hair now entirely white (changed during trial hour).

**Fantine—SLEEPING IN REDEMPTIVE EXPECTATION, TERMINAL ILLNESS ADVANCED**
- Fevered anticipation; sleepless, feverish night filled with happy visions; fell asleep at daybreak; consumption progressing; terminal state (organic disease advanced, life almost despaired of); breathing with tragic sound of fatal maladies; countenance transfigured with ineffable serenity; pallor become whiteness; crimson cheeks; long golden lashes (only remaining beauty); whole person trembling with unfolding wings ready to bear away; resembles something on point of soaring rather than dying; gray hair; sleeping peacefully while Valjean watches.

**Cosette** (Age ~7-8 in 1823)
- At Montfermeil with Thénardiers; not released; medical claims fabricated; bill five hundred-plus francs presented; Fantine believes Madeleine gone to fetch her.

**Thénardier** (Cook-shop keeper, Montfermeil)
- Cook-shop keeper; billing scheme; obstruction of Cosette's departure.

**Javert** (Police Inspector, M. sur M.)
- Recalled by duties to capital of neighboring arrondissement; left courtroom and town after deposition; provided identification testimony via recited deposition; recognized Valjean as "very vicious," suspected Bishop's theft, nineteen years penal servitude, five-six escape attempts.

**Courtroom Witnesses and Officials**
- **Brevet** (Ex-convict, age sixty): business face, prison rascal, recognized Valjean as galley companion entered 1796 left 1815, testified age brutalized him.
- **Chenildieu** (Prisoner-for-life): brought from Toulon galleys, red cassock, green cap, fifty years old, wrinkled frail yellow brazen-faced feverish, nicknamed "Je-nie Dieu," strong glance; bears burn mark on right shoulder and T.F.P. letters from chafing-dish coal attempt.
- **Cochepaille** (Prisoner-for-life): peasant from Lourdes, mountain shepherd turned brigand, savage.
- **Champmathieu** (Accused): made incoherent, impetuous denials; astounded face; laughed at audience laughter; spoke in loud, rapid, hoarse voice with irritated and savage ingenuousness.
- **President** (Court): solemn appeals to witnesses; conducted examination; would have spoken but Valjean interrupted.
- **District-attorney**: conducted interrogation; recited Javert's deposition; demanded witness recall; was interrupted by Valjean's address.
- **M. Bamatabois**: recognized Valjean upon revelation in courtroom.
- **Sister Simplice** (Infirmary): watched Fantine; prepared chinchona potion; perceived Valjean had not come from Montfermeil; suggested delaying Fantine's knowledge of his return.
- **Councillor of Royal Court of Douai**: authorized Madeleine's entry to courtroom.

## Themes
- **Confrontation with past and forced witnessing**: Valjean observing condemnation machinery identical to 1795; watching innocent man condemned in stead; crucifix now present—God present where absent before.
- **Hair-whitening as temporal collapse**: Valjean's gray hair turned white in single hour of trial; Fantine's hair turned gray over two months; physical transformation marks invisible spiritual transformation.
- **Self-revelation and redemptive sacrifice**: Valjean rises to reveal himself; advances toward witnesses; addresses Chenildieu with intimate galley knowledge; allows innocent man to be spared; crowd parts before him as though divine.
- **Sublime spectacle overwhelming human justice apparatus**: Court's machinery of condemnation dissolved into sympathetic witnesses; no questions put, no authority intervened; all felt inwardly dazzled; witnessed "splendid outburst of grand light."
- **Fantine's mystical maternal redemption**: Sleepless night of happy visions; transfigured in sleep; ineffable serenity overspread countenance; trembling with unfolding wings ready to soar; resembles ascension rather than death; Valjean watches beside her as at first visit two months before.
- **Atmospheric doom and inevitability**: Baker's boy late; line at oven long; light went early; ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun on forge wall; frost silvered hedges; children chased hoop; dog barked at nothing; gulls quarreled over fish heads; wind off water with salt and tar smell; bees hummed; bell for vespers; all suggesting inexorable fate now fulfilled.
